observations.prose: The prose addresses the reader as ‘you’ in every piece — not the instructional ‘you’ of a manual, but the ‘you’ of political solidarity. The reader is placed inside the situation being analysed: ‘it is the company’s actions, not the driver’s, that determine whether that driver gets a job’ (2026-07-11-your-risk.txt). Write ‘you’ when the reader is the person on whom the described system operates.

‘We’ appears alongside ‘you’ as a co-sufferer or co-citizen pronoun: ‘We got rid of pop-ups by installing pop-up blockers’ (2026-07-21-dickovers.txt) places writer and reader together in historical action. Use ‘we’ when the claim is collective — something done or endured together — and ‘you’ when the cost falls on the reader individually. These two stances alternate within single pieces without friction.

Contracted forms are the default register of every piece. ‘They won’t share the data,’ ‘it’s flexibility for Uber,’ ‘we’d call AI’s applications plug-ins’ — the contraction appears in nearly every sentence (2026-07-11-your-risk.txt, 2026-07-24-supplemental-income.txt). Write contracted forms throughout; uncontracted negatives belong only to formal or legal quotation reproduced within the text.

Uncontracted negation — ‘do not,’ ‘cannot,’ ‘will not’ — is near-absent across the corpus. Against the dense contracted baseline, an uncontracted negative would register as a formal register the prose never enters. The positive habit this replaces is the contracted form throughout; the assembler reuses that observation here.

When uncertainty is acknowledged, it arrives as a first-person marker rather than a hedging adverb: ‘I think the only reason this question doesn’t come up more frequently’ (2026-07-13-go-meta-meta.txt), ‘I think there’s a whole cohort of investors’ (2026-07-24-supplemental-income.txt). Most claims land without any qualification at all. If you need to hedge, write ‘I think’ or ‘I’d add’; do not reach for ‘perhaps,’ ‘arguably,’ or ‘it could be said.’

Rhetorical questions drive the argument forward and are answered in the next sentence or paragraph. ‘Why would they operate a hospital if they could go meta and sell the doctorbots to the MBAs running the hospital?’ (2026-07-13-go-meta-meta.txt). The question is never left open; it frames an answer the prose has already prepared. Pose the question, then deliver the answer in the sentence that follows it.

Named sources are handed the floor briefly, then extended or corrected: ‘As Weil writes,’ ‘As Quiggin writes,’ ‘As Tim O’Reilly writes’ — the attribution opens the engagement (2026-07-11-your-risk.txt, 2026-07-22-table-flipper.txt, 2026-07-16-lucky-orifices.txt). Opponents are also named directly: Trump, Uber, Thiel. Front-load the name when citing an ally; name the opponent before characterising their position, not after it.

Profanity appears in every piece but is rationed, arriving at the moment of maximum contempt or absurdity: ‘tell the cartel to fuck off’ (2026-07-09-wilhoitian.txt), ‘holy shit, is Uber’s investor relations site seriously serving ASPX pages’ (2026-07-11-your-risk.txt). The expletive marks a rupture in register that signals genuine disgust rather than rhetorical heat. Spend it once; a second use in a piece should feel more earned than the first.

The writer enters as a named individual with history: age, illness, named friends, a daughter’s age. ‘My doctor just informed me that I am cancer free, following excision, radiotherapy and immunotherapy’ (2026-07-14-designated-survivor.txt). These biographical facts are not incidental — they anchor abstract actuarial or strategic claims in personal stakes. Place the biographical detail before the abstract claim it grounds, not as an afterthought.

En-dashes handle mid-sentence interruption and parenthetical elaboration throughout the corpus, with round parentheses serving the lighter asides. Sharp pivots and qualifications that interrupt the main clause use the en-dash: ‘you become painfully aware that there are plenty of people who need your job — who will happily step in to take it’ (2026-07-10-posthuman-as-in-no-humans.txt). Write en-dashes for interruption; not em-dashes.

Em-dashes are absent from every piece in the corpus. The interruption role they would occupy is taken entirely by en-dashes and, for lighter asides, parentheses. Use en-dashes (–) for mid-sentence breaks; do not use em-dashes (—).

Analogies are built from concrete, everyday transactions — restaurants, escrow agents, markets, bears — to explain abstract economic or political structures. ‘Trump is the escrow agent who keeps the money and the deed, then announces he did it because the seller was a fentanyl dealer’ (2026-07-22-table-flipper.txt). The analogy is extended until it collapses under the target’s own absurdity. Choose a familiar transaction, run it until it exposes the logic as incoherent.

Pieces open in one of three shapes: an ironic framing (‘Here’s an irony’ — 2026-07-11-your-risk.txt; ‘Here’s a sentence that stopped me in my tracks’ — 2026-07-22-table-flipper.txt); a term introduced and defined (‘One of 2026’s better tech-related coinages is “dickover”’ — 2026-07-21-dickovers.txt); or a theoretical proposition immediately put under pressure (‘The theory of markets goes like this’ — 2026-07-16-lucky-orifices.txt). None begin with the central claim; all begin with the frame that makes the claim legible.

Closings return to the opening frame or compress the argument’s stakes into a single portable formulation. ‘What they call “theft” is just self-defense’ (2026-07-21-dickovers.txt). ‘Politics aren’t about who rules — it’s about whether we are ruled at all, or whether we are free’ (2026-07-09-wilhoitian.txt). The final paragraph introduces no new evidence; it turns the accumulated argument into a sentence the reader can carry away. End with the sharpest version of the thesis, not a summary of the path taken.

gaps: The voice card was unfilled; all findings derive from the corpus alone. The corpus spans ten consecutive days in a single argumentative register — tech, economics, and politics for a returning readership. How this voice behaves in shorter forms, in fiction, in correspondence, or in sustained scholarly argument is unknown. The biographical self-reference is consistent but narrow in range; whether it deepens or recedes under different emotional conditions cannot be determined here. The round-parenthetical-spans measurement shows heavy parenthetical use across all pieces but no separate observation could be accommodated within the fourteen-observation ceiling; the assembler has the measurement available.
